claims.claim: Kay says the year on The Silmarillion taught him that great works reach their final form through rewriting and mistakes rather than arriving fully formed.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Alison Flood, The Guardian, 29 October 2014
claims.quote: They get there with writing and rewriting and drudgery

claims.feature: other: biography of the Silmarillion year

claims.quote: He had spent a year, between 1974 and 1975, in Oxford

claims.feature: other: silence about the editing method

claims.quote: Kay won't talk about the details of the editing process

claims.claim: Kay says the Silmarillion year demanded a degree of concentration and focus he had not previously exercised as a student.

claims.feature: other: authority conferred by the Tolkien estate work

claims.claim: Kay describes his working method as steeping himself in a historical period and then twisting it slightly.
